title: Sr. Director, KOH Operations
text:
**Sr. Director, KOH Operations**

***Nexpera LLC | Based in Houston, Texas***

Nexpera is an industrial chemistry company serving refining and industrial customers across North America. Our potassium hydroxide business recovers and reprocesses spent KOH from HF alkylation units and other industrial sources, returning specification product to customers who depend on consistent quality and reliable supply. The Sr. Director, KOH Operations leads that business end to end.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Sr. Director, KOH Operations holds single-point accountability for the safe, compliant, and profitable operation of five KOH facilities: Houston, Texas; New Orleans, Louisiana; two sites in the Chicago area; and Tamaqua, Pennsylvania. The role owns safety performance, product quality, cost, asset reliability, and the development of the people who run these plants, while driving the growth of the KOH platform alongside commercial partners.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is comfortable in the plant and credible in front of a customer. The successful candidate will spend meaningful time at each site, will set a visible standard for process safety, and will build an operating rhythm that holds five geographically dispersed plants to one common set of expectations.

**Scope of Responsibility**
---------------------------

Five operating facilities across four states, with the leadership team, operating budget, capital program, and customer relationships that support them.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Safety, Health and Environmental Performance**

Own safety outcomes across all five sites and set the expectation that no production target justifies an unsafe act. Lead process safety management for caustic handling and the associated thermal, pressure, and corrosion hazards, including mechanical integrity, operating windows, management of change, and pre-startup safety review. Ensure each facility maintains its environmental permits and regulatory obligations in good standing, and that incidents, near misses, and high-potential events are investigated to root cause with corrective actions that close on schedule.

### **Operational Execution and Reliability**

Deliver production and on-time delivery commitments across the network, balancing plant capability against customer demand. Establish a consistent operating discipline at all five sites covering shift handover, operating limits, preventive maintenance, and turnaround planning. Drive asset reliability and uptime through disciplined root cause analysis of unplanned outages, and hold the sites to a common standard for maintenance execution rather than letting each plant run its own practice.

### **Product Quality**

Own product quality from feedstock receipt through shipment. Maintain the specification and testing regime that customers rely on, ensure laboratory and analytical capability is sound at each site, and lead the response when a quality deviation reaches a customer. Build the trend data and process controls that prevent repeat excursions rather than catching them at final test.

### **Growth**

Partner with commercial leadership to grow volume and margin in the KOH platform. Identify and unlock latent capacity within the existing asset base, evaluate debottlenecking and expansion opportunities, and provide the operating input that underpins new customer agreements and onsite service offerings. Support evaluation of new facility locations and acquisition opportunities, including the operational due diligence and integration planning that follow.

### **EBITDA Growth and Cost Management**

Build and own the operating and capital budgets for the KOH network, and deliver against them. Manage variable cost per ton, labor, maintenance spend, logistics, and third-party services with an understanding of what drives each. Prepare and defend capital authorization requests, and hold projects to their approved scope, schedule, and cost once funded.

### **People and Organizational Development**

Lead, coach, and develop the site leadership teams, and build the bench that supplies the next generation of plant managers. Set clear performance expectations, conduct meaningful reviews, and address performance gaps directly. Own staffing plans, succession, and the technical training that keeps operators and maintenance crews competent in a caustic-handling environment, and work to make Nexpera a place skilled people choose to stay.

### **Continuous Improvement**

Establish a common set of operating metrics across the five sites and use them to find and close performance gaps. Transfer best practice between plants deliberately rather than by accident, so that a fix proven in Tamaqua reaches Houston and Chicago. Sponsor structured improvement work on yield, energy, cycle time, and labor productivity, and build the expectation at every level that this year's performance is the baseline, not the target.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

Bachelor's degree in chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Twelve or more years in chemical, refining, or process manufacturing operations, including at least five years leading a plant or a multi-site operation.

Demonstrated ownership of safety and process safety performance in a hazardous chemical environment, with working command of PSM elements and OSHA and EPA regulatory obligations.

Full profit and loss or operating budget accountability, including capital planning and project justification.

A record of developing people and building leadership teams, not simply managing them.

Willingness to travel regularly to the four sites outside Houston, estimated at 30 to 40 percent.

### **Preferred**

Direct experience with caustic, potassium hydroxide, or spent-chemical recovery and regeneration processes.

Experience serving refining customers or operating within a customer's fence line.

Multi-site leadership across geographically separated plants.

Formal continuous improvement training, such as Lean or Six Sigma, applied in a process environment.

Advanced degree in engineering or business.

Merger and acquisition integration or greenfield facility startup experience.

**Working Conditions**
----------------------

Based in the Houston office with regular travel to New Orleans, the two Chicago-area sites, and Tamaqua. Time in operating plants requires the use of personal protective equipment and the ability to work around caustic chemicals, elevated temperatures, and rotating equipment. The role carries an on-call expectation for significant operational and safety events across the network.

**Organizational Relationships**
--------------------------------

Close working partnerships are expected with commercial leadership on customer commitments and growth, with EHS on safety and regulatory standards, with supply chain and logistics on feedstock and product movement, with engineering and capital projects on asset investment, and with finance and human resources on budget and staffing.

*Nexpera is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to any characteristic protected by law.*
